title: " Correspondances " fonctorielles. Dualité des topos : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Last page of the 'correspondances fonctorielles / dualité des topos' notes. The previous page set up the Isbell-type picture: A embeds fully in A^ (presheaves) and in A^∨° (opposite of copresheaves), with A = A^ ∩ A^∨°. This page records the universal properties that let one read the same data as sheaves or as cosheaves, and states the resulting 'duality'.

(1) Free cocompletion. For M cocomplete, Hom(A,M) ≃ Hom_!(A^,M). Here Hom_! means colimit-preserving functors (left Kan extension along Yoneda). If M is additive or abelian, this is also ≃ Hom_!(A^_ab, M), where A^_ab is presheaves of abelian groups on A, the free additive cocompletion.

(2) Example M = Ab, with A = B°. Then Hom(B°, Ab) = B^_ab, abelian presheaves on B. The vertical ≃ (unfinished) presumably identifies this with Hom_!(A^_ab, Ab), i.e. cocontinuous functors on the abelian presheaves of the dual category.

(3) Dictionary with A = B°, B = A°. A functor A → M can be read two ways.
- On the A side: Hom(A,M) ≃ Hom_!(A^,M), cocontinuous functors on A^. These are 'cofaisceaux sur A à valeurs dans M' (cosheaves on A^).
- On the B side: the same object is Hom(B°,M) ≃ Hom^!(B^°,M), continuous functors (B^)° → M (right Kan extension). These are 'faisceaux sur B à valeurs dans M'.
So M-valued cosheaves on the presheaf topos of A are the same as M-valued sheaves on the presheaf topos of A°.

(4) General formulas for a topos X.
- F(X,M) means M-valued sheaves, i.e. continuous functors X° → M, written Hom^!(X°,M) (the page writes A for the topos).
- F̌(X,M) means M-valued cosheaves, i.e. cocontinuous functors X → M.
- Since a continuous functor X° → M is the same as a cocontinuous functor X → M°, the page gets F(X,M)° ≃ F̌(X,M°), i.e. Hom^!(A°,M) ≃ Hom_!(A,M°)°.
- It then states F(X,M) ≈ F̌(X°,M), 'F(X,M) et F̌(X,M°) sont duals l'un de l'autre'. Here X° can only sensibly mean the 'dual topos': for X = A^ it is (A°)^. In that case the formula is exactly (3).

Purpose: to define a duality on (presheaf) topoi exchanging sheaves and cosheaves with coefficients in an arbitrary target M. This is the core of 'dualité des topos'.
errors: F(X,M) ≈ F̌(X°,M) is only meaningful if X° denotes a 'dual topos'. This is clear for presheaf topoi, where (A^)^dual = (A°)^, but no construction is given for a general Grothendieck topos. In general such a dual need not exist as a topos; in modern terms it requires dualizability of X in Pr^L.
Hom(A,M) ≃ Hom_!(A^_ab,M) requires M additive (e.g. abelian, cocomplete). This is implicit and not stated.
The second vertical isomorphism in the M = Ab example is left unfinished ('Hom_!(A^_ab' with no closing argument).

ideas.what: Hom(A,M) ≃ Hom_!(A^,M): presheaf category as free cocompletion
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the Yoneda embedding / free cocompletion

ideas.what: Additive version via abelian presheaves A^_ab
M-valued sheaves = continuous functors X° → M; cosheaves = cocontinuous functors X → M; F(X,M)° ≃ F̌(X,M°)
ideas.modern_name: Sheaves with coefficients as limit-preserving functors (Lurie, SAG 1.3.1 style); sheaf/cosheaf duality via opposite coefficients
ideas.where_published: SGA4 has sheaves with values in categories; the cosheaf formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Dual topos: M-valued sheaves on X ≈ M-valued cosheaves on X° (with (A^)° := (A°)^)
ideas.modern_name: Dual of a presentable category in Pr^L (Fun^L(PSh(A^op),M) ≃ PSh(A)⊗M); dualizable presentable categories

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'dualité des topos' is formulated through coefficient-independent equivalences: sheaves on X with values in any M ≈ cosheaves on the dual X° with values in M. This is precisely the characterization of the dual of X in the monoidal category of presentable categories, which the later literature (Lurie, BZFN) formalized as dualizability in Pr^L. There, PSh(A)^∨ = PSh(A^op) and Shv(X) is self-dual for locally compact X (Lurie's Verdier duality, HA 5.5.5). These notes, from 1982 on, appear to anticipate this viewpoint for 1-topoi without the tensor product language.
missed.quote: F(X, M) ≈ F̌(X°, M) ... F(X,M) et F̌(X,M°) sont duals l'un de l'autre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor of dualizable presentable categories and of Verdier duality as Shv ≃ CoShv. It also raises an open thread: which Grothendieck topoi admit a 'dual topos' in this coefficient-free sense. That is related to continuous / exponentiable topoi and to Johnstone–Joyal continuous categories.

deep.surprise_reason: The formulas themselves are routine Kan-extension identities. The notable point is the programmatic framing of a 'duality of topoi' via sheaves ↔ cosheaves with arbitrary coefficients, which prefigures dualizability in Pr^L. The page only treats the presheaf case and gives no general construction.
transcription_corrections: 'M = ab' should read 'M = Ab' (category of abelian groups).
'Hom_♮(A,M) ≃ Hom^♮_!(A^,M)' is better read as 'Hom(A,M) ≃ Hom_!(A^,M)' with an uncertain subscript mark; the following region is crossed out.
The bracketed '[?]' after 'duals' can be read as 'sont duals l'un de l'autre'.
In the left column the lines read F(X,M)° ≃ F̌(X,M°) = (Hom^!(A,M))° = Hom_!(A°,M°); the A here is presumably the topos itself, possibly with a missing ° (Hom^!(A°,M)).
